sources.name: glTF 2.0 / GLB
sources.licenceText: Spec text: CC-BY-4.0 (SPDX tag in repo README source) V. Sample code in the repo: not checked.
sources.use: Master format for meshes, materials, animation. One file, loads in three.js, Blender, Babylon, PlayCanvas.
sources.verdict: adopt. Already the planned master format in R2 [62].

sources.name: KHR extensions
sources.use: Ratified list includes `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `KHR_texture_basisu`, `KHR_texture_transform`, `KHR_lights_punctual`, `KHR_animation_pointer`, `KHR_materials_*` (clearcoat, transmission, volume, sheen, ior, iridescence, anisotropy, dispersion, emissive_strength, specular, unlit, variants), `KHR_gaussian_splatting`, `KHR_interactivity`. `EXT_meshopt_compression` is listed as ratified. `KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness` is archived.
sources.verdict: adopt (use ratified ones only). Avoid archived extensions.

sources.name: Draco
sources.use: Mesh compression library, used by `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`.
sources.verdict: hold. Meshopt is simpler and also lossless-friendly (U). Use Draco only for a very large static mesh.

sources.name: meshoptimizer
sources.use: Mesh and animation compression (`EXT_meshopt_compression`) and simplification.
sources.verdict: trial. Test on one GLB for size and load time.

sources.name: glTF-Transform
sources.use: Node library and CLI to optimise, compress, dedupe, resize textures in GLB.
sources.verdict: adopt for the ingest step (R2 [62] "Normalise").

sources.name: USD / OpenUSD
sources.licenceText: "Tomorrow Open Source Technology License 1.0", an Apache-2.0 variant with a changed trademark section V. No SPDX id found. GitHub reports NOASSERTION V.
sources.use: Scene interchange (Pixar). Only as an export for other tools.
sources.verdict: hold. Interchange only. GLB covers our web needs.

sources.name: three-gpu-pathtracer
sources.use: Path-traced render in three.js, converges by sample count.
sources.verdict: hold. Interesting for stills. Pre-1.0.

sources.name: Blender (Cycles, EEVEE)
sources.licenceText: Source: GPL-2.0-or-later. Cycles: Apache-2.0. Binaries: GPL-3.0-or-later V. Your renders and `.blend` files are yours V.
sources.use: Offline cinematic renders from a `.blend` or a Python script. Molecular Nodes (GPL-3.0, per R2 [62]) runs inside it.
sources.verdict: adopt for offline hero frames and thumbnails (Cycles on CPU or CUDA). EEVEE headless: hold until tested on the WSL/Linux box.

sources.verdict: adopt - chemistry panels.

sources.name: SmilesDrawer
sources.use: Browser SMILES drawer, SVG or canvas.
sources.verdict: trial - lighter than RDKit.js; check bond style.

sources.name: Ketcher
sources.use: Structure editor.
sources.verdict: hold - use to author a molfile, then draw with RDKit.js.

sources.name: opentype.js
sources.use: Reads font files; turns text into outline paths.
sources.verdict: adopt - text to outlines for print SVG (R2 rule).

sources.name: Inter
sources.licenceText: OFL-1.1 V ("Copyright (c) 2016 The Inter Project Authors")
sources.use: Sans-serif UI and figure text.
sources.verdict: adopt - default figure font.

sources.name: IBM Plex
sources.licenceText: OFL-1.1 V ("with Reserved Font Name Plex")
sources.use: Sans, Serif and Mono family.
sources.verdict: adopt - Plex Mono for code and sequences.

sources.name: Source Sans 3
sources.use: Sans-serif body text.
sources.verdict: adopt - second text face if a figure needs one.

sources.name: resvg (extra)
sources.licenceText: MIT (LICENSE-MIT seen) V; dual licence not checked
sources.use: Renders SVG to PNG and PDF-ready bitmaps without Chrome.
sources.verdict: trial - cross-check Chrome output of a figure.

sources.name: D2 (extra)
sources.use: Diagram language with ELK and dagre layouts. Go binary.
sources.verdict: hold - ELK.js gives the same layout without a binary.

sources.name: svg.js (extra)
sources.use: Small SVG builder.
sources.verdict: hold - the kit already builds SVG.

sources.name: rough.js (extra)
sources.use: Hand-drawn style shapes.
sources.verdict: reject - hand-drawn look suits no science figure.

sources.name: Bioicons
sources.licenceText: Per-asset, mixed. README prefers CC0 and MIT; CC BY also occurs. Rule: keep the author and licence of each icon, not "Bioicons". V
sources.use: Lab objects, cells, organisms as SVG. Repackages third-party art.
sources.verdict: trial - ingest per icon, quarantine anything without a clear licence.

sources.name: Health Icons
sources.licenceText: CC0-1.0 for icons and npm packages. Website code MIT. V
sources.use: Clinical pictograms, outline and filled.
sources.verdict: adopt - no credit needed.

sources.name: Reactome icon library
sources.use: Pathway glyphs: receptors, organelles, compounds.
sources.verdict: adopt - pathway figures.

sources.name: Servier Medical Art (SMART)
sources.use: Organs, tissues, cells.
sources.verdict: adopt - exact credit line below.

sources.name: SciDraw
sources.licenceText: CC-BY-4.0 per Zenodo records of single drawings (S). The site page gave no terms text.
sources.use: Neuroscience drawings with a DOI each.
sources.verdict: trial - read each drawing's page and DOI before use.

sources.name: NIAID NIH BioArt
sources.licenceText: Per-asset, mixed. The terms page names no licence; "check the license on each entry". Free for educational, research, informational and commercial use. V
sources.use: Viruses, immune cells, pathogens.
sources.verdict: trial - record the entry licence at ingest.

sources.name: PhyloPic
sources.licenceText: Per-image: CC0-1.0, PDM, CC-BY-3.0, CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-3.0, CC-BY-NC-3.0, CC-BY-NC-SA-3.0. V
sources.use: Organism silhouettes.
sources.verdict: trial - allow CC0, PDM, CC-BY only; quarantine SA and NC.

sources.name: OpenMoji
sources.use: Colour emoji set.
sources.verdict: reject for figures - share-alike and emoji style.

sources.name: Lucide
sources.licenceText: ISC; the Feather-derived icons are MIT. V
sources.use: General UI icons.
sources.verdict: hold - Tabler is already installed.

sources.name: Tabler Icons
sources.use: General UI icons; already a root dependency.
sources.verdict: adopt - already in use.

sources.name: Material Symbols
sources.use: Google UI icons.
sources.verdict: hold - duplicates Tabler.

sources.name: W3C Design Tokens Format Module (DTCG)
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: W3C Community Final Specification Agreement (V). Not on the W3C Standards Track (S)
sources.use: Neutral JSON file format for tokens. Base for the Molecullage theme object.
sources.verdict: Adopt. Stable, vendor-neutral, supported by Style Dictionary, Tokens Studio, Figma, Penpot (V). Note: no `pt` or `mm` unit, so print sizes go in `$extensions`.

sources.name: Style Dictionary
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Reads tokens, writes CSS variables, JSON, JS.
sources.verdict: Trial. Test the colour-object and dimension-object parts on our file. If it fails, a 30-line converter beats waiting.

sources.name: Tokens Studio (Figma plugin 2.13.2; sd-transforms 2.0.3)
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Edit tokens in Figma, sync to Git.
sources.verdict: Hold. Useful only if a designer wants Figma. No Figma in the current flow.

sources.name: Open Props
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: CSS custom-property set: sizes, easings, animations, 19 Open Color hue sets, 16-step oklch palette.
sources.verdict: Trial. Use as a reference for easings and durations and as a test of DTCG export. Do not take its palette.

sources.name: Tailwind CSS v4 (`@theme`)
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Utility CSS. `@theme` turns tokens into CSS variables and utilities (`--color-*`, `--text-*`, `--ease-*`, `--spacing`).
sources.verdict: Trial for the editor only. Figures and films stay plain CSS. Map tokens with `@theme inline`.

sources.name: shadcn/ui (CLI + registry)
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Copy-in React components styled with CSS variables; own registry to share items.
sources.verdict: Trial for the editor. Good model for naming. Needs React and Tailwind.

sources.name: Radix Primitives
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Unstyled accessible React widgets.
sources.verdict: Hold. Base UI covers the same ground and is newer. Keep as fallback.

sources.name: Radix Colors
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: 12-step colour scales. Steps 1-2 background, 3-5 component fill, 6-8 borders, 9-10 solid, 11-12 text (V).
sources.verdict: Trial for editor neutrals. Not for figure colours.

sources.name: Base UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Unstyled React widgets from the Radix, Floating UI and MUI people (V).
sources.verdict: Trial for the editor. Active, v1.

sources.name: Ark UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Headless widgets for React, Solid, Vue, Svelte on Zag.js state machines (V).
sources.verdict: Hold. Multi-framework is not a need today.

sources.name: Park UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Styled kit on Ark UI + Panda CSS (V).
sources.verdict: Reject. No release for 11 months; adds a second CSS system.

sources.name: daisyUI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Tailwind plugin. 35 built-in themes as CSS variables in oklch (V).
sources.verdict: Hold. Its themes are look presets. Molecullage colours have meaning (antigen, binder), so presets do not fit.

sources.name: Material Design 3 tokens + material-color-utilities
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: Apache-2.0 (V). M3 token page text could not be read (page body empty) — U
sources.use: M3 token system; library makes a theme from one source colour (HCT).
sources.verdict: Hold. Dynamic colour changes hue per source, which breaks fixed semantic families. Maybe one use: pick an accent for the editor chrome.

sources.name: Fluent 2 tokens
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: npm package MIT (V). Repo licence field NOASSERTION (V: mixed). Licence of design assets: not found
sources.use: Two layers: global tokens (raw) and alias tokens (meaning) (V). Supports light, dark, high contrast (V).
sources.verdict: Hold. Copy the two-layer idea. No dependency.

sources.name: IBM Carbon tokens
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Themes White, Gray 10, Gray 90, Gray 100. Tokens by role (`$layer-01`, `$border-subtle-01`), component tokens (V).
sources.verdict: Hold. Good naming reference for layers. No dependency.

sources.name: Open Color
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: 13-step hue sets.
sources.verdict: Reject. Stale. Not designed for colour-blind safety.

sources.name: ColorBrewer
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: Apache-2.0 (V, GitHub API); copyright Brewer, Harrower, Penn State (V)
sources.use: Sequential, diverging, qualitative schemes for maps and charts.
sources.verdict: Adopt for data ramps in plots. Keep the credit line.

sources.name: viridis / cividis
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: viridis page: CC0 (V). Cividis paper: CC0 dedication (V)
sources.use: Perceptually even colour maps. Cividis is made for colour-vision deficiency.
sources.verdict: Adopt for continuous data.

sources.name: Okabe-Ito palette
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: Page has no licence. It asks users to credit Masataka Okabe and Kei Ito (V)
sources.use: 8 colours safe for common colour-vision deficiency.
sources.verdict: Adopt for categorical data series. Credit the authors. Check the hex list against a printed source before shipping.

sources.name: Paul Tol schemes
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: No licence or terms on the page (V). `tol_colors.py` licence: not found
sources.use: Qualitative (bright, high-contrast, vibrant, muted, medium-contrast, dark, pale, light), diverging (sunset, nightfall, BuRd, PRGn), sequential (YlOrBr, iridescent, incandescent, smooth/discrete rainbow, banded) (V).
sources.verdict: Trial. Use as reference. Ask Paul Tol or cite before bundling the full set.

sources.name: CSS `color-mix()`, `oklch()`, `light-dark()`, `prefers-color-scheme`
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Make tints and dark variants in the browser from one token.
sources.verdict: Adopt for decks and editor. For print figures, keep sRGB hex in the token and test the PDF.

sources.name: Animate UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: "MIT + Commons Clause" (R1, V). GitHub API shows NOASSERTION (V)
sources.use: Animated Radix/Base UI/React Aria wrappers on Motion.
sources.verdict: Reject (R1).

sources.name: Magic UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Copy-in animated React components via shadcn CLI.
sources.verdict: Reject. Landing-page effects; no seek.

sources.name: Aceternity UI
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: Item licence by Aceternity Labs: unlimited end products, no resale or redistribution as a template (V). Statement that free parts are MIT: S only (third-party directory)
sources.use: Animated React blocks for landing pages.
sources.verdict: Reject. Custom licence, and free tier terms are not confirmed.

sources.name: Motion Primitives
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.use: Motion + Tailwind component snippets.
sources.verdict: Reject. Beta; hover/spring motion.

sources.name: React Bits
sources.section: 2. Table A — themes, tokens and UI kits
sources.licenceText: MIT + Commons Clause v1.0 (V). Key limit: may not sell, sublicense or redistribute the tools or sounds themselves (V)
sources.use: Large set of animated components and effects.
sources.verdict: Reject. Commons Clause blocks redistribution inside a free engine. Effects run on their own clock.

sources.name: Motion (motion.dev, ex Framer Motion)
sources.licenceText: MIT (V, deps.dev and GitHub API). Motion+ is a paid add-on: one-time 399 USD per developer, teams yearly per seat. It adds components (Gallery, Carousel, Ticker, Cursor, AnimateNumber, AnimateText, Typewriter, ScrambleText, AnimateView, Curtains, splitText), examples, an AI kit and "Motion Studio". Its APIs and examples are MIT-licensed. Builder's Licence needed if a product resells Motion+ capability (V)
sources.use: `animate()` for DOM/SVG/values; React hooks.
sources.verdict: Trial as a t-to-value mapper. Do not buy Motion+.

sources.name: GSAP
sources.licenceText: "Standard 'no charge' licence" (Webflow). deps.dev calls it "non-standard" (V). Owner Webflow. Permitted: use "on any website, web application, or digital interface". Prohibited: use "in tools that allow users to build visual animations without code" when such a tool rivals Webflow's animation builder (V, section I "Definitions", gsap.com/standard-license)
sources.use: Timelines, DrawSVG, MotionPath, SplitText, MorphSVG. Already in `stage/`.
sources.verdict: Adopt for the code-driven engine. Hold inside the planned graphical editor until Webflow confirms the clause does not apply. Keep it behind the adapter so anime.js can replace it.

sources.name: anime.js v4
sources.use: Timeline, stagger, SVG, `seek()`.
sources.verdict: Trial as the MIT fallback to GSAP.

sources.name: lottie-web
sources.use: Plays Lottie JSON (After Effects, Jitter export).
sources.verdict: Adopt (SVG renderer) for imported designer clips. Slow release pace; watch it.

sources.name: dotLottie web + ThorVG
sources.use: WASM player for `.lottie` files. ThorVG is the C++ vector engine under it.
sources.verdict: Trial as a second choice to lottie-web. Run the hash-repeat test.

sources.name: Rive
sources.licenceText: Runtime: MIT (V, GitHub API). Editor: closed SaaS. Plans per seat per month: Free 0, Cadet 9, Voyager 32, Enterprise 120 (V). Page says free-plan exports play a Rive splash screen (V). Commercial terms: not found
sources.use: Runtime plays `.riv`; editor makes them.
sources.verdict: Hold. Interactive decks only. Needs editor licence for clean exports.

sources.name: Theatre.js
sources.use: Keyframe editor and runtime.
sources.verdict: Hold. Good model, but no release for 17 months.

sources.name: Remotion
sources.licenceText: Remotion License, deps.dev "non-standard" (V). Free: individuals, for-profit organisations with up to 3 employees, non-profits, evaluators. Company License above that. Pricing page: Automators 0.01 USD per render, min 100 USD per month; Creators 25 USD per seat per month; Enterprise from 500 USD per month (V). License text says it will change slightly in Remotion 5.0 (V)
sources.use: React video renderer with frame-based clock.
sources.verdict: Reject as a dependency. Licence limits a free engine. Molecullage has the same idea.

sources.name: Motion Canvas
sources.use: Generator-based canvas animation editor.
sources.verdict: Reject as a dependency; read for ideas (editor with preview).

sources.name: Revideo
sources.use: Fork of Motion Canvas for headless rendering.
sources.verdict: Reject. Competing engine.

sources.name: Web Animations API (WAAPI)
sources.use: Browser-native animation objects. `element.animate()`; `document.getAnimations()`.
sources.verdict: Adopt. No dependency, works with CSS animations and transitions via `getAnimations()`.

sources.name: CSS scroll-driven animations
sources.use: Link an animation to scroll or view progress (`animation-timeline: scroll()` / `view()`).
sources.verdict: Hold. Not needed; WAAPI gives the same result by time.

sources.name: View Transitions API
sources.use: Animated change between two DOM states (slide change).
sources.verdict: Hold. Fine for live deck slide switches. Film uses its own cross-fades.

sources.name: SMIL (SVG `<animate>`)
sources.use: Animation inside an SVG file. Works in stand-alone SVG output.
sources.verdict: Trial for SVG figures that must carry their own motion.

sources.name: Manim Community
sources.use: Python maths animation, offline video.
sources.verdict: Hold. Optional offline asset for equation clips.

sources.name: Poly Haven
sources.use: Studio lighting images, surface textures and models

sources.name: Sketchfab
sources.licenceText: Per model: CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA, CC-BY-NC and others. Read the label of each model.
sources.use: Ready 3D models; the search is open, the download needs an account

sources.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
sources.use: Experimental structures of proteins, nucleic acids and complexes

sources.name: PubMed
sources.licenceText: Records are free; the licence of each article differs.
sources.use: Find papers and their DOIs. A record gives the abstract only, never the full text.

sources.name: PubMed Central
sources.licenceText: Open full texts; the licence of each article differs.
sources.use: Full texts of open articles, the way to ground a claim

sources.name: HAL open archive
sources.use: Open copies of French research papers. Check that the file body matches the cover page: one deposit held a different paper.

sources.name: 3D ContentCentral (Dassault Systemes)
sources.use: CAD models of lab parts, for example a generic 0.2 mL tube with cap

sources.name: GrabCAD Community Library
sources.use: Free CAD models, including PCR tubes

sources.name: Printables
sources.use: Printable models; mostly accessories such as racks, rarely accurate parts

sources.name: Thingiverse
sources.use: Printable models; mostly accessories

sources.name: NIH 3D
sources.licenceText: Per entry; many are public domain
sources.use: Biomedical models, including lab equipment

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons (3D files)
sources.use: Free 3D files with a clear licence; few in biology

sources.name: Maker data sheets (SPL, Axygen/Corning, Eppendorf, Thermo Fisher, Bio-Rad)
sources.use: Dimensions, materials and volumes of lab consumables, to check a 3D model against

sources.name: RDKit MolDraw2D (ACS-1996)
sources.use: 2D chemical structures in ACS-1996 style from checked SMILES; rdDetermineBonds rebuilds connectivity from 3D coordinates

sources.name: SAMSON (OneAngstrom)
sources.use: 3D molecular complexes, sticks and balls-and-sticks with soft studio lighting and clear camera

sources.name: Molecular Nodes (Blender 5.2+)
sources.use: Import PDB, mmCIF and trajectories into Blender Geometry Nodes for Cycles and EEVEE studio rendering

sources.name: Open Babel
sources.use: Convert chemical file formats, generate 3D coordinates and perceive bonds for typed contacts
